TIGRAY · 13:06 UTC

Tigrayan leaders say new war with Ethiopian govt has begun

Tigray sits inside Ethiopia's federal system as the northernmost regional state. Its ruling party the Tigray People's Liberation Front held national power for nearly three decades until 2018 when Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed sidelined it and later fought a two-year war against it that ended with the Pretoria peace deal signed in November 2022.
On September 24 the TPLF announced that federal forces had opened a new round of fighting. Its fighters seized the airport at the regional capital Mekelle and clashed with government troops on the eastern border with the Afar region. The move followed months of rising friction between Mekelle and Addis Ababa and came one day after the TPLF declared an alliance with other groups that stated its goal of removing the prime minister from office.
The federal government has not yet issued an official confirmation of the reported clashes. The situation now turns on whether the Pretoria agreement's disarmament and power-sharing terms hold or whether the new fighting spreads beyond the Tigray-Afar border.
